verdict.rationale: Phoenix documents an SDK API reference with modular Python SDK packages, including span querying. It also documents client SDKs for prompts and Python/TypeScript SDKs for evaluations against traces and datasets, so the product can be driven programmatically through its own documented interfaces. However, the evidence never shows a documented REST/HTTP API reference, and the OpenAPI probe returned 404 on all candidate paths (those were arize.com root paths, not a Phoenix instance, so this is not a concrete contradiction). Missing for 10: an explicit public REST/HTTP API reference or OpenAPI spec, documented auth and endpoint coverage across all resources, and independent hands-on corroboration of API use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Spans — Query and analyze traces with powerful filtering capabilities
Phoenix's Python SDK is modular by design, allowing you to install only what you need. Each package serves a specific purpose and can be used independently or together.
Phoenix offers client SDKs to keep your prompts in sync across different applications and environments.
Python and TypeScript SDKs for running evaluations against Phoenix traces, datasets, or any data source.
